clue.text: Gunmen grabbed guards in charge of arms

indicators.note: the word for grabbed surrounds and protects the gunmen, as a guard encloses

parts.note: to have grabbed something is to have held it
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the army's gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men seize the security staff who look after the weapons store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' looks like weapons, but here it means coats of arms; 'guards' is the container signal, and the Royal Artillery are the army's gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic describes coats of arms and the study of armorial bearings.

clue.text: Flogging papers in Mercury houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the chemical symbol encloses the rest

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Seems to describe newspapers being sold off inside the Mercury publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging' hints at selling, but it is a beating; 'houses' is the container signal around the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a thorough beating or thrashing.

clue.text: Pull out of plant storing some DNA from the south

indicators.note: storing means keeping inside, so the herb holds the genetic word

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: a gene is a stretch of DNA

explanation.surface: Pull out from a plant some of its genetic material, sampled from its southern side.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'from the south' means read upwards, giving ENEG; 'storing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue (renege) is to go back on a promise, to withdraw from a commitment.

clue.text: Lenin wasn't prepared for activity in court

indicators.note: prepared suggests made up or arranged afresh, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: The revolutionary Lenin was unready to face a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a sports court.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the formal name for the racket sport played on a court.

clue.text: Independent "at home" almost split posh top celebs

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to divide is to split
U denotes upper-class, posh usage
the A-list is the top rank of celebrities

explanation.surface: A newspaper at home splits a posh list of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' looks like the newspaper title; it is a noun for a free spirit. 'Almost' cuts DIVIDE to DIVID.
explanation.definitionFit: An individualist is a person who thinks and acts independently, a nonconformist.

clue.text: Two coppers join game

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper and P a penny, an old British copper coin
to tie things is to join them

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers link up for some sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but gives the metal's symbol CU and P for a penny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a knockout match in a football cup competition.

clue.text: Push prow of gondola into river

indicators.note: into places the front letter inside the river name

parts.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Steering a gondola's front out into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge is to press or drive someone forward, to push.

clue.text: One very loudly boarding transport upset cars?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the whole combination is reversed
boarding means getting on, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a cart transports goods
I is the Roman numeral for one
FF, fortissimo, means very loudly in music

explanation.surface: A noisy passenger climbing aboard upsets the car's occupants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boarding' gives CIFFART, which 'upset' turns over; the question mark flags cars as an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is vehicles moving on roads collectively, so cars are an example; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Director and judge can't stand

parts.note: an exec, executive, is a company director
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A director and a judge who cannot bear each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't stand' looks like a physical inability; it is loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or loathe, to be unable to bear.

clue.text: Made notes, more than needed for study

indicators.note: the clue words contain more letters than the answer requires, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: Someone over-diligently took notes beyond what was required for their study.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'Made' and the start of 'notes'; 'more than needed' says those words hold surplus letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a private room for work or reading, a study.

clue.text: Tiered display of piping at the match?

definitions.text: Tiered display of piping at the match?

parts.words: Tiered display of piping at the match?
parts.note: the piping is decorative icing, and the match is a marriage rather than a sporting fixture

explanation.surface: Seems to describe banks of seating for a pipe band performing at a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping' suggests bagpipes and 'match' a game; read them as icing piped on and a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional celebration confection is built in tiers and decorated with piped icing at a marriage reception.

clue.text: On cue, visitors spread out, scoffing 19

indicators.note: spread out means scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Guests arrive on cue and fan out, gobbling flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is DIPTERA, the flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Insectivorous means feeding on insects; eating flies fits.

clue.text: Running down info about militancy, ignored by clubs

indicators.note: about tells us the word for info is turned round

parts.note: GEN is British slang for information

indicators.note: the clubs abbreviation is left out of the word for militancy

parts.note: activism is militant campaigning
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Intelligence on political militancy is disparaged and overlooked by the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns GEN into NEG; 'ignored by' removes C from ACTIVISM, leaving ATIVISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Negativism is a habit of disparaging or rejecting things, constantly running them down.

clue.text: A bunch of flyers withdrawing some way off

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the airmen's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a body of flyers

explanation.surface: A flock of birds retreating into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyers' suggests birds, but the bunch is the Royal Air Force; 'withdrawing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a distance, a long way away.

clue.text: Play area secured ground to start again

parts.note: a rec, recreation ground, is a play area

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: A playground made secure so play can resume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a field; it is a past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To recrudesce is to break out again after dormancy, as a disease does.

clue.text: Shooting star, such as Brezhnev

definitions.meaning: a meteor from the November shower radiating from Leo
The first name of Brezhnev, Soviet leader

explanation.surface: Brezhnev presented as a rising celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid names both a meteor of that annual shower and a Russian man such as Brezhnev.

clue.text: Ship's company reduced clipper's work

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew
to have cut something is to have reduced it

explanation.surface: The crew of a sailing ship has been cut back in number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipper' suggests a fast sailing ship, fitting the crew; here it is a barber with clippers.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short hairstyle produced by a barber using clippers.

clue.text: Little river, the tenth causing disease

parts.note: small means little
the Po is Italy's longest river
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A small river, a tithe of the water, spreading disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallpox is an eradicated contagious viral illness.

clue.text: Island produced one member of academy

parts.note: made means produced
I is the Roman numeral for one
RA denotes a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An island turned out one artist elected to the academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic off Morocco.

clue.text: Flies lower, right into drink

parts.note: to dip is to lower

indicators.note: into places the letter inside the beverage word

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone flies low, banking right into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like a verb; it is the insect order.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the insect order of two-winged flies.

clue.text: One put out, claiming rights to break in

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the rights abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: out signals the letters of put are disordered

parts.note: R abbreviates right, doubled for plural

explanation.surface: A single person put out by being forced to assert their rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' makes UPT, and 'claiming' takes the rights inside; 'put out' reads as annoyed in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force one's way in suddenly.

clue.text: Spin dry theatre ruffle

indicators.note: spin means turn round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
rep, repertory, is a theatre

explanation.surface: Reads like a laundry list: spin cycle, tumble dry, a theatrical ruffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' reverses BRUT + REP.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to unsettle or agitate them.

clue.text: British see about masking trendy name on article

indicators.note: masking means covering, so the reversed see encloses trendy
about tells us the cathedral city is turned round

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese, a bishop's see
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A British observer covers up a fashionable name on a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a diocese, Ely; 'about' reverses it to YLE, and 'masking' puts IN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline is the line naming the writer of a newspaper piece.

clue.text: Left work early, primarily to run

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of early is taken

explanation.surface: Someone left the office early, mainly in order to go jogging.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with a long, easy bounding stride.

clue.text: Rowdy underworld boss gets hospital attendant

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god ruling the underworld
an orderly is a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: A gangland chief takes on a hospital porter, sounding like a crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' points to gangsters; it is Dis, Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means unruly and noisy, as in drunk and disorderly.

clue.text: What egotist refers to repeatedly in behavioural trait

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word is said twice

parts.note: an egotist talks about me

explanation.surface: An egotist keeps talking about themselves, a behavioural trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a cultural behaviour or idea passed on by imitation.

clue.text: Prior brings in shelter for five affected

indicators.note: brings in, paired with for, says a shelter word enters the word in place of something
for completes the swap: the shelter word stands in place of the five numeral

parts.note: previous means prior
V is the Roman numeral for five
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: A monastic prior offers refuge to five people who are pretending to be something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings in' and 'for' swap V in PREVIOUS for TENT. 'Prior' looks like a monk; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious and affected both describe showy, artificial behaviour meant to impress.

clue.text: Arm revolutionary centre in seizure

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the chosen letters are read backwards
centre in picks the central letters of seizure

explanation.surface: A rebel weapon at the heart of a coup or seizure of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre in' takes IZU from the middle of seizure; 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, an example of a firearm.

clue.text: Looked into wrong sign always blocking road

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the word for always sits inside road's abbreviation

parts.note: aye is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: Someone examined a misleading road sign that keeps blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong sign' is the cross marking an error, and 'blocking' is the container signal; aye is an old word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: To be X-rayed is to be examined internally, peered inside by radiography.

clue.text: Gather hash in island heading back

the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island of Napoleon's exile
a hash is a mess

explanation.surface: Collect a hashed meal on an island before heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' gives ELBMESSA, which 'heading back' reverses; Elba is the island of Napoleon's first exile.
